page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-288-metal is a bare-metal compute server built around Intel Xeon 6985P-C processors. The architecture delivers 144 physical cores and 288 dedicated vCPUs operating at speeds up to 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 instruction set. Memory provisioning is substantial, featuring 2232 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 6 GHz, which provides approximately 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU, coupled with 504 MB of shared L3 cache.

Hardware capabilities include Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX-TILE, AMX-INT8) and AVX-512 vector processing support. As a bare-metal deployment, the server operates without hypervisor overhead, providing direct physical access to execution cores and memory channels. The configuration contains no discrete GPU accelerators and includes no local storage, requiring persistent workloads to utilize networked storage infrastructure.

Benchmark results highlight top-decile performance in multi-threaded computation, PassMark CPU benchmarks, and memory throughput, with large-block memory read bandwidth exceeding 1090 GB/s. High-concurrency throughput is evident from database operations reaching over 423 million Redis SET operations per second and strong parallel compilation metrics. Sequential CPU performance is standard, while large language model text generation remains modest due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware.

The server offers high hardware density suitable for organizations running memory-bound and multi-core enterprise applications. Primary workload fits include large in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, intensive batch ETL data processing, and large-scale parallel software compilation suites.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-288-metal is a bare-metal server configured with 288 dedicated vCPUs across 144 physical cores using Intel Xeon 6985P-C processors at speeds up to 4.2 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with 504 MB of L3 cache, it integrates 2232 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, achieving a memory density of 7.75 GB per core. The system contains no integrated GPUs and provides no local storage, relying on external network storage. Benchmark evaluations highlight exceptional multi-core throughput, top-tier memory bandwidth surpassing 1090 GB/s on large uncached reads, and high performance in database operations with over 423 million Redis SET operations per second. However, CPU-based text generation remains constrained compared to GPU accelerators. Given its massive memory footprint and raw multi-threaded capacity, this server is engineered for large in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, parallel software compilation, and extensive batch processing pipelines.
